note: PRICES CHANGE. This table was checked against the providers' pricing pages on the as_of date and WILL drift. Every cost in the ledger is an estimate derived from this table applied to the usage numbers the provider returned; it is not a bill. Rows carrying a `note` were not on the provider's pricing page when it was last looked at (the note gives the day) and are kept, unverified, only so older ledgers stay priced. Override or extend the table with ~/.calas-gateway/prices.json (same shape; models merge over these) and check `calas-gateway doctor`, which warns when this table is older than 60 days.

anthropic.match: A request model is priced only when it equals a key, or a key plus -latest or a date (-YYYYMMDD or -YYYY-MM-DD): claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 -> claude-sonnet-4-5. Any other id is unpriced, never guessed from a similar name (claude-opus-4-9 is not claude-opus-4).

openai.match: Same rule: a key, or a key plus -latest or a date (gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 -> gpt-4.1; gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 -> gpt-4.1-mini, the longer key). Any other id is unpriced (o3-pro is not o3, gpt-5-pro is not gpt-5).
openai.cache_writes: OpenAI reports cache writes as usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens (Responses API; the same name is parsed under prompt_tokens_details if Chat Completions ever sends it). GPT-5.6 and later bill them at 1.25x the uncached input rate, given per row as cache_write; GPT-5.5 and earlier have no additional cache-write charge, hence the provider multiplier of 1 (plain input price).
openai.long_context: Prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at the long_context tier for the whole request (2x input and cache rates, 1.5x output) on the models that list one.
